extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and early-career writers (bloggers, freelance writers, and fiction writers)
extracted.subtask_description: General how-to guidance for beginning writers covering daily habits, craft study, publishing first work, freelancing steps, and recommended writing tools. Targets writers who want practical, actionable steps to improve and launch a writing career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write every day / daily writing habit
rubrics_metrics.description: Start by writing every day — even 300–500 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes daily practice as the primary way to become a writer; consistency over perfection. Related guidance on finishing drafts and building experience from regular output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write daily without editing as you go
rubrics_metrics.description: The most effective writing tips for beginners are: write daily without editing as you go...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid self-editing during initial drafts to maintain momentum and complete work; editing comes later in revision stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish what you start / complete first drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: Most importantly, finish what you start — completing a first draft matters more than making it perfect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise completion of drafts to build experience and material to revise or publish later; completion is a key metric of progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read widely in your genre and study craft books
rubrics_metrics.description: Read widely in your genre and study craft books like Stephen King's On Writing or William Zinsser's On Writing Well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reading both to learn conventions and to internalize craft; studying recommended craft books helps develop technique and perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study one craft book at a time
rubrics_metrics.description: Study one craft book at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on a single craft resource to avoid overwhelm and to apply lessons more effectively before moving to another book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get feedback from real readers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit responses from actual readers (peers, critique groups, early audience) to learn what works and where to improve; feedback is listed as one of the most effective tips for beginners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish first work on a blog or Medium to gain experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish first work on a blog or Medium. Experience comes from doing, not waiting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use accessible publishing platforms to build a track record and learn the publishing/revision cycle; early publication is positioned as practical experience-building rather than waiting for perfect work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build 3–5 writing samples and create a simple portfolio
rubrics_metrics.description: To start freelance writing, build 3–5 writing samples, create a simple portfolio...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A small set of polished samples demonstrates capability to potential clients and is the foundation of a freelance pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch to small publications in your niche
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch to small publications in your niche. Platforms like Contently, Mediabistro, and ProBlogger list paid writing opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target smaller outlets to gain clips and experience; use niche-focused pitching to improve acceptance chances and build credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical beginner freelance rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Beginner rates typically start at $0.05–$0.15 per word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a market benchmark for novice freelancers when negotiating or setting expectations; useful for rate-setting and evaluating offers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended software and tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Most professional writers use Scrivener for long-form drafting, Google Docs for collaboration, and Grammarly or ProWritingAid for editing. AI writing tools like Claude and ChatGPT are increasingly used for research and first drafts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific tool recommendations tied to tasks: Scrivener for long-form drafting, Google Docs for collaborative work, grammar tools for editing, and AI as an assist for research/drafting. Use tools to support workflow rather than replace craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use writing prompts to overcome writer's block
rubrics_metrics.description: 300+ Writing Prompts to Break Through Writer's Block (resource listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ curated prompts to generate material, restart momentum, and practice different styles or scenarios when stuck.
